properties.foundation_analysis: The subterranean stratigraphy consists of Carboniferous sedimentary bedrock of the Strathclyde Group (Gullane Formation sandstone and siltstone) mantled by stiff lodgement till. Structural lithics are dominated by pale cream-to-buff Craigleith sandstone—a dense, highly siliceous Carboniferous quartz-arenite—interspersed with Hailes and Cullalo sandstone for rear courses and basements. Structural joints are pointed with traditional natural hydraulic lime (NHL 2/3.5) and sharp quartz sand. The Prince Albert Memorial sits on a monumental tiered plinth of igneous Peterhead pink granite. The undulating topography slopes gently north-northwest toward the Water of Leith, facilitating natural subsurface gravity drainage across glacial drift.

properties.primary_surfacing: Engineered roadway and paved pedestrian curbs
properties.wear_characteristics: Authentic environmental patina and drainage grading

properties.botanical_analysis: Parkland garden trees inside the square comprise mature deciduous specimens of *Acer pseudoplatanus* (Sycamore), *Ulmus glabra* (Wych Elm), and *Tilia × europaea* (Common Lime). Grounded in late-December winter phenology, all canopies exhibit complete defoliation, revealing intricate bare branch networks, dark wet bark, dormant terminal buds, and exposed skeletal silhouettes.

properties.architectural_summary: A formal Georgian urban composition terminating the western vista of George Street. In the immediate center stands the Prince Albert Memorial (1876, Sir John Steell), featuring a monumental bronze equestrian figure atop a multi-tiered polished granite plinth with projecting stepped pedestals bearing subsidiary bronze figure groups. The architectural backdrop is dominated by West Register House (formerly St George's Church, 1811–1814, Robert Adam / Robert Reid), defined by a monumental Neoclassical front with a colossal Greek-order portico, projecting entablature, and an elevated circular colonnaded peristyle drum supporting a ribbed hemispherical copper cupola crowned by a stone lantern and finial. Flanking the central civic core are symmetrical Georgian terraced wings (Charlotte Square west facade), unified as palatial pavilions: three principal storeys over a rusticated basement and attic with pitched dormered roofs, rigorous 6-over-6 timber sash-and-case fenestration grids, modillioned cornices, and planar ashlar frontages.
